source.version: Metadata only (Crossref, OpenAlex, and Semantic Scholar, independently read on 2026-10-09); no abstract or full text obtained. Crossref identifies Information Technology and Management, volume 27, issue 3, pp. 383-398, published online 2025-04-17 and in print 2026-09. Crossref supplies no abstract; OpenAlex has abstract_inverted_index=null and no open-access full text; Semantic Scholar has abstract=null with a publisher-elision disclaimer and supplies only a machine-generated TLDR. Europe PMC returned no DOI record and the arXiv title query returned no results. Both Springer article and PDF endpoints returned Client Challenge; no bot check was bypassed. No markdown conversion, full document, appendices, or PDF pages could be read.
source.title_on_document: Generating creativity through ChatGPT: an empirical investigation in open innovation platforms

paper_design_summary: Only bibliographic metadata and a machine-generated Semantic Scholar summary were accessible; no abstract or full text was obtained. The title concerns ChatGPT and creativity in open innovation platforms, but design, assignment, population, AI use, tasks, and outcomes remain unverified. The single study entry is a placeholder and does not establish the complete study inventory.

open_questions: Obtain an abstract or full text to establish all studies, assignment procedures, and analyzed people counts; core eligibility remains unclear.
Verify the task and complete output-outcome inventory, including any novelty, originality, similarity, or diversity measure, before assigning a context class.
Verify the population, platform, sample period, number of users and works, and how ChatGPT availability or individual use was measured.
notes: The Semantic Scholar TLDR is machine-generated, not the paper's text. The triage note describing difference-in-differences and participation, work length, complexity, and votes remains an unverified lead. The study entry and other-valued design, assignment-unit, count-type, AI-role, and task fields are placeholders, not confirmed design details; an empty outcome list does not establish that qualifying outcomes are absent. Title and author entries come from metadata, not an inspected document. Page count 16 is derived from the Crossref page range 383-398, not an observed PDF page count (https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1007%2Fs10799-025-00454-5, message.page). Crossref author strings are Li Yongjun, Li Xinyue, and Wang Lizheng; OpenAlex normalizes the first and third as Yongjun Li and Lizheng Wang, while Semantic Scholar lists Yongjun Li, Xinyue Li, and Li-Zhen Wang. All six checker corrections concern evidential certainty. Their audit quotes are null because no paper passage was accessible; locators identify the independently checked records.
